correctness.rationale: Because sums of two incidences have digits 0,1,2 and their encodings are bounded by 2 max S < n, equality of all empty, single and two-step sums agrees before and after encoding. The merge relations reduce any face generator to singletons, and the incidence map shows there are no further singleton relations. The kernel N of the map from Z^d to Z/n is finite index, of rank d, since the first singleton step is 1. On the lattice digraph an upward threshold clamp deletes at most one coordinate from every incidence step, keeping it allowed by downward closure or making it stationary. Consecutive clamps have pointwise vertical singleton arrows or coincidences. The integral signed prism between them takes allowed paths to allowed paths modulo stationary degeneracies and induces the chain homotopy on Ω, by the prism boundary identity. Finitely many clamps in each coordinate contract the finite support of every reduced cycle; global uniform boundedness is not needed. The only forbidden terms in a boundary of an allowed word are internal two-step deletions; they preserve the start vertex, and coincidences among their increment words are exactly the short equalities already compared. Thus the same finite-rank free integer kernel W_m occurs at each start in the lift and quotient. The lifted augmented Ω is a free Z[N]-resolution (translation by N is free on starts), and its coinvariants identify with quotient Ω without assuming that coinvariants in general preserve kernels. The integral Koszul resolution of this deck group gives the claimed exterior groups, including H_0=Z and vanishing beyond d. Independently replayed pair-sum counts and signed top-cycle cancellations for the three sample graphs give pairings 150, 162 and 1752. Multilinearity of the determinant, with merged vectors equal to sums, provides the cochain identity for all parameters.
residual_risks: The separate modular Fourier block checks mentioned in RESULT.md are not supplied by the bound script/output and were not relied on. The universal integral proof, not the finite pairings or modular arithmetic, carries the exact homology and torsion statement.
No statement is made for wraparound moduli, non-downward-closed families, or a different digraph homology theory.

originality.rationale: The covering mechanism, the field singleton case and the Koszul endpoint are known. The checked circulant theorems either assume no merges/unique unordered two-sums or require acyclicity of the lift over a coefficient field. These results do not prove acyclicity for a general incidence downset with legal merges and collisions. The uniform integral lift and consequent exterior groups for the full family retain a distinct scientific contribution on the inspected evidence.
residual_risks: A prior equivalent acyclicity criterion for downset-step lattice digraphs or a specialization not captured in the inspected statements may exist. A catalogue miss does not certify novelty.

value.rationale: These are natural families of cyclic digraphs whose shortcuts encode arbitrary incidence faces. Both legal merges and collisions can change chain constraints, so their uniform inability to alter the integral path homology (including torsion) is substantive. The integral clamp argument supplies a reusable criterion on finite-support chains and addresses a wide class beyond isolated singleton steps, not just a few numerical examples.
residual_risks: The result is not an assertion of topological or path-homotopy equivalence after arbitrary shortcut additions.
